findings.title: Incorrect dark-theme color transform for embedded topic meta link
findings.body: This replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The first argument should remain `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and the dark alternative should be `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`. As written, light themes get a much lighter link and dark themes get a much darker link, reducing contrast in the embedded-post topic metadata.

findings.title: Dark/light arguments reversed for custom-message-length
findings.body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The correct theme-aware form is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, but this patch uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` as the light-theme value and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` as the dark-theme value. This reverses the intended contrast and is inconsistent with the desktop modal.

findings.title: Topic map h3 color changed to 50% instead of 20%/80% theme pair
findings.body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The dark-theme equivalent should be `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)`, giving `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`. This patch uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, making the mobile topic map h3 significantly lighter in light themes and losing the intended contrast and hierarchy against h4.

findings.title: Group member name uses wrong lightness values
findings.body: This was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, so the theme-aware replacement should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. It is currently `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which removes the intended emphasis distinction from the 50%-lightness title and changes the rendered color in both themes.

findings.title: Group member name uses wrong lightness values on mobile
findings.body: This was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, so the theme-aware replacement should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. It is currently `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which removes the intended emphasis distinction from the 50%-lightness title and changes the rendered color in both themes.

findings.title: Badge notification background has low contrast with its text in dark themes
findings.body: `.badge-notification` sets `color: $secondary`. In a dark theme, `dark-light-choose` returns the second argument here: `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`. Because `$secondary` is the dark background color in such themes, the background remains relatively dark while the text remains `$secondary`, producing dark-on-dark badges with insufficient contrast. The dark-theme background needs to be light, or the text color must be adapted for this base badge.
